plan.estimand: difference in means between two independent normal populations
plan.hypothesis: one-sided test of equality of means; H0: μ_treatment ≤ μ_control vs H1: μ_treatment > μ_control (or equivalent directional formulation)
assumptions: Both groups follow independent normal distributions
Equal variances in both groups (pooled variance t-test)
Observations within and across groups are independent
Test is one-sided with directional alternative
scientific_notes: Power is the probability of rejecting H0 given the alternative is true (effect = 4.3 dBA)
Pooled t-test is appropriate under equal variance assumption

answer.summary: The power of a one-sided pooled t-test comparing two independent normal means with 32 participants per group, an expected difference of 4.3 dBA, common standard deviation of 7.8 dBA, and significance level α = 0.05 is approximately 0.704 (70.4%).
answer.method: Two-sample pooled Student's t-test (one-sided). Power computed using the closed-form formula implemented in R's power.t.test() function, which calculates the cumulative probability of rejecting H₀ under the alternative hypothesis given the specified effect size, standard deviation, sample size, and significance level.
assumptions: Both groups follow independent normal distributions
Equal variances in both groups (homoscedasticity assumption for pooled variance t-test)
Observations within and across groups are independent
Test is one-sided with directional alternative hypothesis (H₁: μ₁ > μ₂)
Significance level α = 0.05 (two-tailed rejection region concentrated into one tail)
limitations: Power depends critically on the normality assumption; violations may alter actual power
The equal variance assumption should be checked; if violated, Welch's t-test may be more appropriate
Actual power is sensitive to the true effect size; if the observed effect differs from 4.3 dBA, power will differ
No adjustment for multiple comparisons if conducted alongside other tests

executions.code:
# Load required package
library(stats)
library(jsonlite)

# Define study parameters
effect_size <- 4.3          # Expected difference in means (dBA)
common_sd <- 7.8            # Common standard deviation (dBA)
n_per_group <- 32           # Sample size per group
alpha <- 0.05               # Significance level
sidedness <- "one.sided"    # One-sided test

# Compute standardized effect size (Cohen's d)
cohens_d <- effect_size / common_sd

# Use power.t.test function for two-sample t-test
# power.t.test with n, delta, sd, sig.level, and type="two.sample"
# For one-sided test with alternative="one.sided"
power_result <- power.t.test(
  n = n_per_group,
  delta = effect_size,
  sd = common_sd,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)

# Extract power
computed_power <- power_result$power

# Display results
cat("=== Power Calculation for Two-Sample Pooled t-Test ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Effect size (difference in means): %.2f dBA\n", effect_size))
cat(sprintf("Common standard deviation: %.2f dBA\n", common_sd))
cat(sprintf("Standardized effect size (Cohen's d): %.4f\n", cohens_d))
cat(sprintf("Sample size per group: %d\n", n_per_group))
cat(sprintf("Total sample size: %d\n", 2 * n_per_group))
cat(sprintf("Significance level (alpha): %.4f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("Test type: One-sided pooled t-test\n"))
cat(sprintf("Computed Power: %.6f\n", computed_power))

# Output in required format
results <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "power", value = computed_power, unit = "probability")
  )
)

cat("\n")
cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(toJSON(results, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))
